problem: Implement solve(s: str) -> int: return the length of the longest contiguous substring containing no repeated Unicode code points.
constraints: Python string elements are code points, not grapheme clusters.
Target O(n) time; explain auxiliary space.
acceptance_criteria: Correct on empty, repeated and mixed inputs.
The left boundary never moves backwards.
O(n) expected time with dictionary access and O(min(n, alphabet size)) auxiliary space.
Accept any correct alternative satisfying the contract.
hints: Consider a window that contains no repeated code point.
Track the last position at which each code point occurred.
A previously seen character must not move your left boundary backwards.
followups: Why is the total work linear rather than quadratic?
What changes if the input is a one-pass stream?
How would grapheme-cluster semantics change the input preprocessing?
source: Original repository teaching fixture; not a benchmark or a real candidate transcript. Offline checks are reported separately.
